question: does answer-checking beat predict-only routing once the high tier is much pricier?

price_ratio.definition: high-tier price / medium-tier price, input and output scaled together; low, medium, extra and the checker keep their real price_as prices

caveats: The whole effect rests on about 11 wrong medium answers out of 117 validation prompts (the checker flags 6, misses 4, 1 unknown, 1 false alarm); one or two prompts more or less move every crossover.
Settings (tau, skip_above) are chosen on validation and reported on validation, which overstates results; an untouched split is needed before believing any number here.

Only price is varied. Real providers with a large price gap also differ in the quality gap between tiers and in answer lengths (tokens), which change both who gets answers right and what each answer costs.
R scales the high tier's price only; the checker stays at groq-small's price, so checking gets relatively cheaper as R grows. A pricier checker would push any crossover higher.
